aberts_squirrel: They do not hibernate, so they stay busy in snowy forests all winter long.
Their fur is gray with a reddish stripe on the back, and their tails are big and fluffy.
aberts_towhee: Abert's towhees live in pairs that stay together all year long.
They have a black face patch around the bill and a cinnamon-colored belly.
acorn_woodpecker: They live in noisy family groups that work together to fill and guard their acorn trees.
Their call sounds like they are laughing 'waka-waka-waka' through the oak woods.
african_giant_snail: They carry their home on their back and can seal their shell shut to stay moist in dry weather.
Each snail is both male and female, so any two snails can lay eggs.
aggregating_anemone: They can clone themselves by splitting in two, making big groups of identical twins.
Tiny algae living inside them use sunlight to make food, which gives them a greenish color.
allegheny_mountain_dusky_salamander: It has no lungs at all, like other salamanders in its family.
Mother dusky salamanders curl around their eggs to guard them until they hatch.
amargosa_toad: Like other toads, they lay their eggs in long jelly strings in the water.
Amargosa toads are most active at night, when the desert air is cooler.
american_alligator: A mother alligator gently carries her babies in her mouth down to the water.
Alligators can grow new teeth to replace old ones that wear out, many times over their lives.
american_avocet: Their heads and necks turn a rusty orange color in breeding season and fade to gray in winter.
Their long blue-gray legs let them wade into deeper water than many other shorebirds.
american_badger: American badgers have long front claws made for digging, like built-in shovels.
Their black-and-white striped faces make them easy to recognize.
american_beaver: They slap their flat tails on the water to warn their family about danger.
Their ears and nose can close tight when they swim underwater.
american_bison: Bison roll in dust and dirt, called wallowing, to shake off bugs and shed their winter coat.
Baby bison are called red dogs because they are born with a reddish-orange coat.
american_black_bear: They are great tree climbers, using their short curved claws to scramble up trunks.
They eat mostly plants, like berries, nuts and grasses, plus some insects.
american_bullfrog: Bullfrogs are the biggest frogs in North America.
Male bullfrogs make a deep call that sounds like 'jug-o-rum'.
american_bumble_bee: Only the queen survives winter, and she starts a brand-new colony each spring.
Their fuzzy bodies help keep them warm, so they can fly on cool, cloudy days.
american_cockroach: They can feel tiny puffs of air with two little feelers on their rear, helping them dodge danger fast.
Their cockroach relatives have been scurrying around Earth since before the dinosaurs.
american_coot: They pump their heads back and forth as they swim, like they are bobbing to music.
Their white bills and dark bodies make them easy to spot, and they often gather in big flocks.
american_copper: American coppers are small butterflies, about the size of a quarter with wings open.
Their caterpillars munch on sorrel and dock plants.
american_crow: They can use sticks and other objects as tools to get food.
A group of crows is called a murder, and in winter thousands may sleep together in one roost.
american_dipper: They bob up and down on rocks all day, which is how they got the name dipper.
They have a see-through extra eyelid that works like swim goggles underwater.
american_goldfinch: Males turn bright lemon yellow in spring and fade to a dull olive color in winter.
They eat almost only seeds, even feeding their babies mashed-up seeds instead of bugs.
american_herring_gull: Young herring gulls are brown and take about four years to get gray and white feathers.
Herring gull chicks peck the red spot on a parent's bill to ask for food.
american_kestrel: Kestrels often pump their tails up and down while perched on wires.
Males have blue-gray wings, while females have rusty brown wings.
american_lady: Its caterpillars hide inside little tents they make from silk and leaves.
Its caterpillars love to munch on fuzzy plants called everlastings and cudweeds.
american_lobster: They have blood that is clear or bluish, not red like ours.
They taste and smell with tiny hairs on their legs and antennae.
american_mink: American minks have thick, oily fur that keeps them warm and dry in cold water.
They are part of the weasel family, along with otters and badgers.
american_oystercatcher: Its bright orange-red bill and yellow eyes make it one of the easiest beach birds to spot.
Its chicks can walk and leave the nest just a day or two after hatching.
american_pika: Pikas are close cousins of rabbits, even though they look like round little mice.
They make a loud squeaky 'eeep' call to warn neighbors and mark their rocky home.
american_red_squirrel: They are smaller than gray squirrels and have a white ring around each eye.
They sometimes dry mushrooms by tucking them on tree branches before storing them.
american_robin: Robins lay eggs of a bright blue color so famous it's called 'robin's egg blue'.
Robins often sing very early in the morning, sometimes before the sun comes up.
american_snout: When resting, it looks just like a dead leaf, and its snout looks like the leaf stem.
Its caterpillars munch on the leaves of hackberry trees.
american_toad: They catch bugs with a super quick flick of their sticky tongue.
Toads lay their eggs in long strings of jelly that can hold thousands of eggs.
american_white_pelican: They are among the biggest birds in North America, with wings about 9 feet across.
Unlike brown pelicans, they do not dive; they dip their pouches from the surface while swimming.
american_wigeon: American wigeons have short bills that are great for nibbling plants, like geese do.
Males make a cheerful three-note whistle instead of a loud quack.
anhinga: They spread their wings wide in the sun to dry because their feathers soak up water.
They spear fish with their sharp, pointy bill, then flip them up to swallow them headfirst.
annas_hummingbird: They can hover in midair and even fly backward by beating their wings super fast.
Its tiny heart can beat over 1,000 times a minute when it is busy flying.
apapane: Its wings make a whirring sound when it flies, so you can hear it zoom by.
Its curved black bill is the perfect shape for reaching nectar deep in flowers.
arctic_green_sea_urchin: Its mouth is on the bottom of its body, and its five teeth are called 'Aristotle's lantern'.
Sea otters and some fish love to munch on green sea urchins.
arctic_ground_squirrel: During hibernation they wake up every few weeks to warm up for a short time.
In summer they stand tall on their back legs to watch for danger.
arctic_tern: They chase summer at both ends of the world, so they see more daylight than any other animal.
They hover over the water and then dive down to snatch small fish.
arizona_gray_squirrel: They have big bushy tails edged in white that they use for balance and shade.
They munch on walnuts, acorns, and pine seeds and bury extra food to eat later.
arizona_mantis: Arizona mantises hold their front legs folded up, which makes them look like they are praying.
Their green or brown colors help them hide among leaves and twigs.
arizona_toad: Like other toads, they have dry, bumpy skin and hop in short little jumps.
They hide in damp ground during the day and come out to hunt bugs at night.
aromatic_cherry_millipede: Despite the name millipede, it has far fewer than a thousand legs, two pairs on most body parts.
They help forests by munching on dead leaves and turning them back into soil.
asian_house_gecko: They can drop their tail to escape danger, and a new tail grows back.
They love hanging around porch lights at night, waiting to catch insects drawn to the glow.
asian_lady_beetle: Asian lady beetles come in many colors, from yellow to orange to red, with lots of spots or none.
In fall, they often gather on sunny walls looking for a warm place to spend winter.
asian_shore_crab: They came to the US from Asia, probably as tiny babies carried in ships' water.
Females carry their eggs tucked under their bodies until they hatch.
asian_spinybacked_orbweaver: Its tiny body is wider than it is long, a bit like a little crab with horns.
Like other spiny orbweavers, the males are much smaller than the females.
atlantic_blue_crab: Its scientific name, Callinectes sapidus, means beautiful savory swimmer.
Males have bright blue claws, and females have claws with red tips.
atlantic_ghost_crab: Atlantic ghost crabs dig deep burrows in the sand and come out mostly at night.
Their pale, sandy color makes them seem to vanish on the beach, just like ghosts.
atlantic_horseshoe_crab: Its long pointy tail helps it flip back over if a wave turns it upside down.
It has ten eyes, including two big ones on the sides of its shell.
atlantic_lions_mane_jelly: They have no brain, heart, or bones, and their bodies are mostly water.
Small fish sometimes swim among their tentacles to hide from bigger fish.
atlantic_puffin: Their bright orange bill colors are brightest in summer, and part of the bill falls off in winter.
They dig burrows in the ground for nests and use their feet like little shovels.
atlantic_rock_crab: Its shell is covered in tiny reddish or purple speckles.
Like all crabs, it molts its old shell so it can grow bigger.
atlantic_sand_crab: They have no big claws and catch food with feathery antennae as waves wash past.
They move up and down the beach with the tides to stay in the wave zone.
atlantic_sand_fiddler_crab: They pick food from sand and roll the leftovers into tiny balls that dot the beach.
They dig burrows in the sand and hide inside when the tide comes in.
autumn_meadowhawk: They are small dragonflies, about as long as your finger.
Pairs often fly linked together while the female taps eggs into the water.
bald_eagle: Bald eagles are not really bald; the name comes from an old word for white-headed.
The bald eagle is the national bird of the United States.
baltimore_oriole: They love sweet fruit and nectar, and they often visit orange slices left out for birds.
Males are bright orange and black, while females are a softer yellow-orange.
banded_tussock_moth: Its caterpillars have long hair tufts at both ends that look like little paintbrushes.
Its caterpillars munch on leaves of many trees, like oak, maple, and walnut.
banded_watersnake: They are strong swimmers that hunt fish and frogs in ponds, swamps and streams.
Females give birth to live baby snakes instead of laying eggs.
barn_owl: Barn owls have heart-shaped faces that catch sound like a satellite dish.
Instead of hooting, barn owls make a loud, raspy screech.
barn_swallow: Barn swallows catch flying insects in midair, zooming low over fields and water.
Their long, forked tails help them twist and turn quickly in flight.
barred_owl: They have no ear tufts, so their round heads look smooth.
Barred owls sometimes hunt in daytime and even catch crayfish and fish.
barrows_goldeneye: Males have a white crescent-shaped patch on their faces, just in front of their golden eyes.
They dive underwater to find snails, insects, and other small food on the bottom.
bat_star: Bat stars get their name from the webbing between their arms, like a bat's wings.
They have tiny tube feet on their undersides that help them crawl along the sea floor.
bay_nettle: Like all jellies, it has no brain, no heart and no bones.
Its body is mostly water, which is why it looks see-through.
beldings_ground_squirrel: They give sharp alarm calls to warn their relatives when a hawk or coyote is near.
They live in high mountain meadows and are often called picket pins because they stand so straight.
belted_kingfisher: They dive headfirst into water to catch fish, then fly back to a perch to eat.
They dig long tunnels into dirt banks by rivers to make their nests.
big_brown_bat: Big brown bats find food in the dark by making sounds and listening for echoes.
Big brown bats sometimes roost in barns and attics, and many hibernate in winter.
bighorn_sheep: Rams crash horns together in contests so loud they can be heard far away.
Their split, rubbery hooves grip rocks, so they climb steep cliffs with ease.
birch_shield_bug: They mostly sip juices from birch and alder trees.
Like other shield bugs, it can let out a stinky smell to keep enemies away.
black_and_gold_bumble_bee: They are some of the largest bumble bees in North America.
Like other bumble bees, they can buzz their bodies to shake pollen loose from flowers.
black_bellied_whistling_duck: Black-bellied whistling-ducks have bright pink-red bills and long pink legs.
They often nest in tree holes, and families stay together for a long time.
black_billed_magpie: Its long tail can be as long as its whole body.
Its black feathers shine green and blue when sunlight hits them.
black_bullhead: Black bullhead parents guard their babies, which swim together in a tight dark ball.
They can live in muddy, warm ponds where many other fish could not survive.
black_capped_chickadee: In fall they grow new brain cells that help them remember where they hid food.
They can lower their body temperature on cold nights to save energy.
black_chinned_hummingbird: Its throat looks black, but in good light a purple band shines at the bottom.
Its nest is made with soft plant fluff and spider silk, so it can stretch as the chicks grow.
black_crappie: Black crappies feed most at dawn, dusk and night.
Males sweep out nests on the lake bottom and guard the eggs.
black_crowned_night_heron: Adults have bright red eyes that help them spot food in dim light.
Their call is a loud, barking 'quok!' often heard at dusk.
black_guillemot: In winter, their black feathers turn mostly white with speckles.
They use their wings to flap and fly underwater while chasing small fish.
black_headed_grosbeak: Black-headed grosbeak dads help keep the eggs warm and even sing while sitting on the nest.
Their name means 'big beak', which is perfect for crunching seeds and bugs.
black_kingsnake: Its shiny black scales help it soak up the sun's warmth.
Like other kingsnakes, it squeezes its food to catch it instead of using venom.
black_leather_chiton: It slowly grazes on algae, scraping rocks with a tongue covered in tiny teeth.
When pulled off a rock, a chiton can roll up into a ball like a pill bug.
black_legged_kittiwake: They are named for their call, which sounds like someone saying kittee-wayke.
They spend most of the year far out at sea, only coming to land to nest.
black_necked_stilt: Compared to its body, it has some of the longest legs of any bird.
Stilts wade in shallow water and pick tiny bugs and shrimp with their needle-thin bills.
black_oystercatcher: Pairs often stay together for years and return to the same nesting spot.
They have pink legs and bright yellow eyes ringed in red.
black_phoebe: They often pump their tails up and down while perched.
They like to live near water and catch flying insects in midair.
black_skimmer: Its pupils can narrow into slits like a cat's eyes, helping it handle bright sunlight on water.
They often feed at dusk and night, when the water is calm and fish come near the surface.
black_slug: Black slugs can be black, brown, orange or even reddish, despite their name.
When startled, a black slug can scrunch into a round hump and rock from side to side.
black_swallowtail: Its caterpillar can pop out a pair of orange 'horns' that give off a stinky smell.
Young caterpillars look like bird droppings, which helps keep them safe.
black_tailed_bumble_bee: They are one of the first bumble bees to come out in early spring.
They help pollinate wildflowers, fruit trees, and berry bushes.
black_tailed_jackrabbit: They are actually hares, not rabbits, and their babies are born furry with eyes open.
They can run very fast and leap far with their long, powerful back legs.
black_tailed_prairie_dog: Prairie dogs are not dogs at all; they are a kind of ground squirrel.
Prairie dogs do a 'jump-yip' where they leap up and call out, and others join in.
black_throated_sparrow: They have a bold black bib and two bright white stripes on their face.
Their tinkling songs ring out across the desert in spring.
black_triggerfish: Triggerfish can lock a spine on their back upright to wedge themselves safely into rock cracks.
They often swim by waving their top and bottom fins instead of their tail.
black_turban_snail: They live in tide pools and munch on algae with a rough, scraping tongue.
Their shells are dark purple-black and shaped a bit like a little turban hat.
black_vulture: Black vultures help keep nature clean by eating leftovers that other animals leave behind.
They often soar in groups and follow each other to find food.
black_witch: Its wings can be almost as wide as a grown-up's hand.
It flies at night and often rests in dark corners during the day.
blackbanded_darter: Darters have no swim bladder, so they sink and dart from rock to rock instead of floating.
They eat tiny insects and larvae they find between pebbles on the stream floor.
blackspot_sergeant: They are named for a black spot near the base of the tail fin.
Like other damselfish, the males guard their eggs and chase away hungry fish.
blackstripe_topminnow: Its top-facing mouth is perfect for grabbing food at the water's surface.
Many have a shiny gold or silver spot on top of their heads.
blanchards_cricket_frog: They are tree frogs that almost never climb, staying at the water's edge instead.
They can skip across the water's surface in a few quick hops.
blandings_turtle: Its dark shell is sprinkled with yellow flecks, like stars in the night sky.
They have a hinge on their bottom shell so they can partly close up.
blue_banded_hermit_crab: Their legs have bright blue bands near the tips, which is how they got their name.
They live in tide pools and help clean up by eating bits of dead plants and animals.
blue_billed_white_tern: White terns have big dark eyes and snowy white feathers that glow against blue skies.
Their chicks are born with strong feet to hold tight to the bare branch where they hatch.
blue_copper: Like other copper butterflies, it is small and quick and loves sunny open places.
Its caterpillars munch on wild buckwheat plants.
blue_dasher: Its huge eyes wrap around its head, giving it nearly all-around vision.
Young blue dashers live underwater as nymphs before climbing out to become flyers.
blue_grosbeak: They often spread and flick their tails while perched.
Young males take about a year to become fully blue, looking patchy brown and blue in between.
blue_jay: Blue jays can copy the call of a red-tailed hawk.
Blue jays love acorns and bury many of them, which helps plant new oak trees.
blue_spotted_salamander: Its dark body is sprinkled with light blue spots, like specks of paint.
They lay eggs in spring pools that dry up later, so no fish live there.
blue_winged_teal: In spring, males have a bold white crescent on their face.
A pale blue patch on their wings flashes when they fly.
bluegill: They have a dark blue-black flap on the edge of the gill cover, which gives them their name.
Males often nest close together in big groups called colonies.
boat_tailed_grackle: Boat-tailed grackle males are shiny black, while the females are warm brown.
They live along coasts and marshes and often walk boldly around parking lots.
bobcat: They have black ear tufts and spotted coats that help them hide in the brush.
They are about twice the size of a house cat and are great climbers.
bobolink: Males wear a black suit with a creamy yellow patch on the back of the head, like a backward tuxedo.
Its bubbly song sounds a bit like a happy robot or R2-D2.
boisduvals_blue: Their caterpillars eat lupine plants, so these butterflies live where lupines grow.
Males have shiny blue wings on top, while females are mostly brown.
bold_jumping_spider: Bold jumping spiders don't build webs to catch food; they stalk and pounce instead.
Their mouthparts often shine a bright metallic green or blue.
bonapartes_gull: They are among the smallest gulls in North America and fly lightly like terns.
In summer adults wear a black hood, which turns into a small dark ear spot in winter.
boreal_chorus_frog: They are among the first frogs to call in spring, sometimes while ice is still on ponds.
They usually have three dark stripes running down their backs.
brahminy_blindsnake: They spend most of their lives underground, eating ant and termite eggs and larvae.
They are sometimes called flowerpot snakes because they travel the world hiding in potted plants.
brant: Brant spend their summers nesting far north in the Arctic tundra.
They are the smallest of the sea geese, only a bit bigger than a mallard.
brewers_blackbird: They walk around on the ground, bobbing their heads like chickens, to find seeds and bugs.
They often nest in groups, building their nests close to their neighbors.
brickwork_woodlouse: Woodlice breathe through gill-like parts, so they need damp places to stay healthy.
Mother woodlice carry their eggs in a pouch under their body until the babies hatch.
broad_billed_hummingbird: Males have glittering green bodies and a shiny blue throat.
Like other hummingbirds, they can hover in place and even fly backwards.
broad_headed_skink: Broad-headed skinks are good climbers and often live in trees.
Young broad-headed skinks have bright blue tails that fade as they grow up.
broad_tailed_hummingbird: Males show off with high, swooping U-shaped dive displays.
On cold mountain nights they go into torpor, a deep sleep that saves energy.
broad_winged_hawk: They ride warm rising air called thermals so they can soar without much flapping.
They spend summers in forests and fly all the way to South America for the winter.
brook_stickleback: They have about five small sharp spines on their backs to help protect them.
Males turn very dark, almost black, during breeding season.
brook_trout: Brook trout have red spots with blue halos sprinkled along their sides.
Their wormy-looking back markings are called vermiculations.
brown_anole: It can drop its tail to escape a predator, and then grow a new one.
It bobs its head up and down like it is doing push-ups to say 'this is my spot!'
brown_bear: Brown bears have a big shoulder hump made of muscle that helps them dig.
Grizzly bears are a kind of brown bear, and cubs stay with their mom for about two years.
brown_belted_bumble_bee: They often nest on or near the ground, sometimes in thick grass.
Like other bumble bees, they can buzz their flight muscles to shake pollen loose from flowers.
brown_headed_cowbird: Cowbirds got their name from following herds of cows and bison to catch bugs they stir up.
Male cowbirds have glossy black bodies and chocolate-brown heads.
brown_headed_nuthatch: Their squeaky calls sound like a rubber ducky toy.
Young birds from last year sometimes help their parents raise new chicks.
brown_lipped_snail: Their shells come in many colors like yellow, pink and brown, with or without dark bands.
Like other land snails, they glide along on a smooth layer of slime.
brown_pelican: They are the only pelicans that dive from the air into the water to catch fish.
Their pouches can hold much more than their stomachs, so they drain out water before swallowing.
brown_rat: Rats are very smart and can learn their names and simple tricks.
Rats make happy chirping sounds, almost like laughing, when they play.
brown_thrasher: It often sings each phrase twice before moving on to the next one.
Its bright yellow eyes and long curved bill help it flip leaves to find bugs.
brown_trout: Brown trout came to America from Europe in the 1880s.
They have golden-brown sides dotted with black and red spots, often with pale rings around them.
budgerigar: Budgies come from Australia, where wild ones are green and yellow and fly in huge flocks.
They are chatty birds, and some pet budgies can learn to say many words.
bufflehead: Buffleheads are among the smallest diving ducks in North America.
Males have a big white patch on their puffy heads that shines purple and green.
bumblebee_millipede: When bothered, they curl into a tight spiral to protect their soft legs.
Like other millipedes, they eat dead plants and help turn them back into soil.
burrowing_owl: They often move into old burrows dug by prairie dogs or ground squirrels.
Unlike most owls, they are often awake and active in the daytime.
bushtit: They travel in chatty flocks, and at night they huddle close together to stay warm.
They are tiny gray birds that weigh about as much as a few paper clips.
bushy_tailed_woodrat: Bushy-tailed woodrats have fluffy tails, a lot like a squirrel's.
They build big nests of sticks in rocky cliffs and caves.
by_the_wind_sailor: Its sail points left or right, so winds can push different groups in different directions.
It is a deep blue color, which helps it blend in with the ocean.
cactus_wren: They are the largest wrens in the United States.
They get most of the water they need from the insects and fruit they eat.
calico_crayfish: They can live in muddy ponds and ditches, and dig burrows when water dries up.
Like other crayfish, they shed their hard shell as they grow, then grow a bigger one.
california_condor: Condors are scavengers, which means they help clean up nature by eating leftovers.
Condors can soar for hours on warm rising air, barely flapping their huge wings.
california_ground_squirrel: They live in burrow colonies and chirp or whistle to warn each other of danger.
When they spot a snake, they wave their tails and can even warm them up as a signal.
california_gull: They often nest in big colonies on islands in lakes far from the ocean.
Adults have a red and black spot near the tip of their yellow bill.
california_kingsnake: Many have bold black-and-white bands, but some have stripes running down their backs instead.
They squeeze their prey like a hug, then swallow it whole.
california_mantis: California mantises have super-sharp eyes for spotting moving bugs.
Mantis moms lay their eggs inside a foamy case that hardens to protect them.
california_mussel: They live packed together in huge beds on rocky shores pounded by waves.
They filter tiny bits of food out of the seawater when the tide is in.
california_newt: When scared, it arches its back to show off its bright orange belly as a warning.
California newts return to the same pond or stream where they hatched to lay eggs.
california_quail: They live in groups called coveys that can hold dozens of birds.
One quail often stands guard on a perch while the others eat, ready to call an alarm.
california_scrub_jay: They are bright blue and gray with no crest on their heads.
Like other jays, they are noisy and clever, and often call out loudly from treetops.
california_sea_hare: Sea hares got their name from two ear-like tentacles on their heads.
Scientists study their big nerve cells to learn how memories form.
california_sea_lion: They are very noisy and bark loudly, especially when crowded together.
Sea lions have little ear flaps you can see, unlike true seals.
california_tortoiseshell: They spend the winter as adults, tucked away in cracks and logs.
Their caterpillars eat the leaves of ceanothus shrubs, also called wild lilac.
california_towhee: California towhees are plain brown birds with a rusty patch under the tail.
Pairs often stay together for years and call to each other with sharp chip notes.
canada_goose: Its babies, called goslings, can swim the day after they hatch.
They honk to each other while flying to help the flock stay together.
canada_jay: They make sticky spit to glue bits of food into tree bark for winter.
They lay their eggs in late winter, while snow still covers the ground.
canadian_tiger_swallowtail: They live in northern forests and fly in late spring and early summer.
Their caterpillars have big fake eyespots that make them look like small snakes.
canadian_toad: Like many toads, it has bumpy skin and puffs itself up when it feels scared.
Males sing a soft trilling call in spring to attract mates.
cane_toad: Cane toads are one of the largest toads in the world.
They have big glands behind their eyes that make poison, so pets should keep away.
cannonball_jellyfish: They have no long tentacles, just a round dome shaped like a ball.
Tiny spider crabs sometimes ride along on them like a moving home.
canyon_towhee: They are plain brown birds with a rusty patch under the tail.
They often hop around in pairs and stay with their mates all year.
canyon_tree_frog: Canyon tree frogs have sticky toe pads that help them cling to steep rock walls.
They often rest in shady rock cracks near streams during the hot day.
caribou: Their big wide hooves work like snowshoes and help them paddle when they swim.
They travel farther each year than almost any other land animal.
carolina_chickadee: They often hang upside down from twigs to search for insects and seeds.
On cold nights they puff up their feathers and shiver to stay warm.
carolina_mantis: They can change color between brown and green after molting to blend in.
Females lay eggs in a foamy case that hardens and protects the eggs all winter.
carolina_wren: Carolina wrens often hold their tails cocked up as they hop around.
Carolina wrens sometimes nest in odd places like flower pots, boots, or mailboxes.
cascade_golden_mantled_ground_squirrel: They have a golden-brown 'mantle' of fur on their heads and shoulders.
They hibernate through the snowy winter in underground burrows.
cave_salamander: They are bright orange or red with black spots.
Like other lungless salamanders, they breathe through their skin.
cedar_waxwing: They have tiny red waxy tips on some wing feathers, which gives them their name.
They love fruit so much that they can eat berries all day long.
celery_leaftier_moth: Celery leaftier moths are small, plain brown moths often seen flying near porch lights.
Their caterpillars eat many kinds of plants, not just celery.
channel_catfish: Its whiskers, called barbels, help it find food in muddy water.
It has smooth skin with no scales.
checkered_white: Its caterpillars eat plants in the mustard family.
This butterfly loves open, sunny places like fields and vacant lots.
chestnut_backed_chickadee: They have a rich chestnut-brown back and sides, unlike other chickadees.
They like to feed high in tall conifer trees, searching branches for tiny insects.
chestnut_munia: Chestnut munias have thick bills made for cracking seeds.
They have rich brown bodies and shiny black heads.
chihuahuan_green_toad: Their bright green skin with black spots helps them hide among plants.
Males sing a buzzy, insect-like trill to call females to rain pools.
chihuahuan_spotted_whiptail: This whiptail is all female, and moms lay eggs that hatch without any dads.
They hunt by poking their noses into the ground and leaf litter for insects.
chipping_sparrow: In spring they wear a bright rusty cap on their heads.
Their song is a fast, dry trill that sounds a bit like a sewing machine.
chiricahua_leopard_frog: Chiricahua leopard frogs have dark spots on their backs, like a leopard.
Like other frogs, they start life as tadpoles swimming in water.
chital: They often follow monkeys, munching on leaves and fruit the monkeys drop.
They give sharp alarm barks to warn other animals that danger is near.
cinnamon_teal: Females are brown and speckled, which helps them hide while sitting on their nest.

clarks_nutcracker: It has a special pouch under its tongue to carry lots of pine seeds at once.

clarks_spiny_lizard: Its scales are pointy and rough, like a tiny pinecone.
It often climbs trees and moves to the far side of the trunk to stay hidden.
clay_colored_sparrow: Clay-colored sparrows often nest low in shrubs in open, grassy places.
They have a pale brown cheek patch outlined with darker lines.
clearnose_skate: It has see-through patches on each side of its snout, which give it its name.
Skates glide over the sea floor by flapping their wide fins like wings.
cliff_chipmunk: They often sit on high rocks and make loud chipping calls.
Like other chipmunks, they store food in their burrows to eat during winter.
cliff_swallow: Cliff swallows build their nests from hundreds of tiny mud pellets carried in their bills.
They have a pale square patch on the forehead that looks like a headlight.
cloudless_sulphur: Its long tongue lets it sip nectar from deep tube-shaped flowers.
Its green or yellow caterpillars blend in with the leaves they eat.
coast_horned_lizard: Horned lizards love to eat ants and can gobble up lots of them in a day.
Its flat, spiky body helps it blend in with sand and rocks.
collared_peccary: They have a pale band of hair around the neck that looks like a collar.
They can eat prickly pear cactus, spines and all.
colorado_checkered_whiptail: Its body is covered in a neat checkerboard pattern.
Whiptails are fast, busy lizards that flick their tongues as they hunt for insects.
columbia_spotted_frog: Their bellies and legs can be yellow, orange or red underneath.
Their eyes point slightly upward, helping them peek out while floating.
columbian_ground_squirrel: They live in big colonies and whistle loud alarm calls when danger is near.
They fatten up all summer so they can live off their body fat while they sleep.
common_atlantic_slippersnail: They have a small shelf inside the shell, making it look like a tiny slipper.
They catch food by filtering tiny bits from the water instead of crawling to find it.
common_bottlenose_dolphin: Bottlenose dolphins breathe air through a blowhole on top of their heads.
They live in groups called pods and work together to find food.
common_buckeye: It loves to bask in the sun with its wings spread open on bare ground.
Males guard a sunny spot and fly out to check on anything that passes by.
common_chuckwalla: Chuckwallas are vegetarians that munch on desert flowers, leaves, and fruit.
They bask on warm rocks in the morning sun to heat up before starting their day.
common_coqui: They have no webbing on their toes, but sticky toe pads help them climb.
Baby coquis hatch from eggs as tiny froglets, skipping the tadpole stage.
common_desert_centipede: Like all centipedes, it has one pair of legs on each body section.
Its bright colors are a warning to other animals to stay away.
common_eastern_bumble_bee: They are one of the most common bumble bees in the East.
Like all bumble bees, they store small amounts of honey in little wax pots.
common_eastern_firefly: Fireflies make cold light, so their glow doesn't make them hot.
Females answer the males by flashing back from the grass.
common_eider: They are the largest ducks in the Northern Hemisphere.
They dive to the sea floor and swallow mussels and clams whole, shells and all.
common_four_clawed_gecko: Four-clawed geckos can change their skin from dark to pale to match their surroundings.
They are active at night and often hang around lights to catch bugs.
common_gallinule: It has long toes that help it walk on floating plants.
It has a bright red forehead shield and a red bill with a yellow tip.
common_garter_snake: Garter snakes give birth to live babies instead of laying eggs.
In winter, many garter snakes snuggle together in one underground den to stay warm.
common_golden_mantled_ground_squirrel: It has a coppery golden head and shoulders, like it is wearing a mantle.
It hibernates through the winter in an underground burrow.
common_goldeneye: Goldeneyes have bright golden-yellow eyes, which gives them their name.
Goldeneyes nest in tree holes, and the ducklings jump out to the ground a day after hatching.
common_grackle: Grackles have bright yellow eyes that make them look surprised.
Sometimes they let ants crawl on their feathers, which may help keep them clean.
common_loon: Loon chicks often ride on their parents' backs.
Unlike most birds, they have solid, heavy bones that help them dive.
common_merganser: Females have a shaggy rusty-brown head that looks like messy hair.
They nest in tree holes, and the ducklings hop down to the ground soon after hatching.
common_murre: Common murres use their wings to 'fly' underwater while diving for fish.
Common murres nest packed tightly together on bare cliff ledges, with no nest at all.
common_myna: They are brown birds with yellow skin around the eyes and bright yellow legs.
They walk on the ground instead of hopping like many other birds.
common_periwinkle: It has a little trapdoor on its foot that closes its shell when the tide goes out.
Periwinkles can survive out of water for a long time at low tide.
common_pill_woodlouse: They breathe with gill-like parts and need damp places to stay alive.
They help the garden by eating dead leaves and turning them back into soil.
common_raven: Ravens are super smart and can solve puzzles to get food.
Ravens make many sounds, from deep croaks to knocks, and can even copy other noises.
common_ribbon_snake: Its tail is extra long, making up about a third of its body.
Ribbon snakes give birth to live babies instead of laying eggs.
common_ringlet: Adults sip nectar from flowers in grassy meadows and fields.
common_rough_woodlouse: They help keep soil healthy by eating dead leaves and rotting wood.
Mothers carry their eggs in a pouch under their bodies until the babies hatch.
common_sagebrush_lizard: Common sagebrush lizards love to bask on rocks and logs to warm up in the sun.
They have tiny, spiny scales and are often seen darting between sagebrush bushes.
common_sea_star: It has a tiny eye spot at the end of each arm that can sense light.
It can push its stomach out of its body to eat clams and mussels.
common_shiner: They have shiny silvery scales that flash in the sun, which gives them their name.
They often swim in schools in clear streams and eat insects that fall in.
common_shiny_woodlouse: They have a glossy gray shell, often with pale patches along the sides.
They hide under logs and stones during the day and come out at night to eat.
common_snapping_turtle: Snapping turtles can live for many decades.
They spend lots of time resting on the bottom of ponds with just their nose poking up to breathe.
common_spotted_whiptail: Their whip-like tails are much longer than their bodies.
They poke their noses into leaves and soil to sniff out insects.
common_striped_woodlouse: Woodlice aren't insects; they are crustaceans, related to crabs and shrimp.
They love damp places and help recycle dead leaves into soil.
common_tern: They have black caps on their heads and bright red-orange bills in summer.
Males bring fish to females as a gift during courtship.
common_wall_lizard: Common wall lizards came to the US from Europe and now live in a few places here.
They love sunny stone walls, where they bask to warm up.
common_waxbill: It has a bright red stripe through its eye, like a little mask.
These tiny finches eat grass seeds and love to bathe together.
common_whitetail: Males guard a patch of pond and chase other males away.
Females have brown wings with three dark bands on each wing.
common_yellowthroat: Its song sounds like it is saying witchity-witchity-witchity.
It likes to hide low in thick, wet plants like cattails and tall grass.
convergent_lady_beetle: It has two white lines on its back that point toward each other, which gives it its name.
Gardeners like them because they eat aphids that harm plants.
coopers_hawk: Short wings and a long tail help Cooper's hawks steer like a pilot.
Female Cooper's hawks are bigger than the males, and many now live in towns.
copes_gray_treefrog: Its call is a fast, high trill, quicker than the look-alike gray treefrog.
They have bright yellow-orange patches on their inner thighs that flash when they jump.
costas_hummingbird: They are tiny hummingbirds that live in deserts and dry scrublands.
Their purple throat feathers flare out to the sides like a mustache.
couchs_spadefoot: Couch's spadefoots have a hard spade on each back foot for digging backward into soil.
Their tadpoles grow into little toads in just a couple of weeks, before the puddles dry up.
coyote: Their howls and yips help family members find each other and talk.
They eat almost anything, from mice and bugs to fruit and berries.
coypu: Coypu are big rodents that came from South America.
Its nostrils can close underwater and it can stay under for several minutes.
creek_chub: Males grow little bumps called tubercles on their heads during spawning season.
They have a small black spot at the front of the back fin.
cross_orbweaver: Before making a new web, it often eats its old one to recycle the silk.
This spider came from Europe and is also called the garden spider.
cuban_tree_frog: They can change color from pale gray to dark brown or green.
They are not native and came from islands in the Caribbean.
curve_billed_thrasher: Its loud call sounds like a sharp 'whit-wheet!'
It often builds its nest in spiny cholla cactus to keep its eggs safe.
dark_eyed_junco: People sometimes call them snowbirds because they show up in many yards in winter.
They mostly hop on the ground, looking for seeds.
dark_flecked_garden_sunskink: Dark-flecked garden sunskinks originally came from Australia.
They love warm sunny spots in gardens and hunt for tiny bugs in leaf litter.
day_octopus: It has three hearts and blue blood.
It hunts during the day, which is unusual for an octopus.
deertoe_mussel: Baby mussels hitch a ride on fish gills for a short time before settling on the bottom.
Freshwater mussels move by sticking out one muscular foot and pulling themselves along.
dekays_brownsnake: They are often found in backyards and city parks, hiding under rocks and boards.
Females give birth to live babies instead of laying eggs.
desert_blonde_tarantula: Tarantulas grow very slowly, and females can live for over 20 years.
In late summer and fall, males wander far to find mates.
desert_collared_lizard: It has two black collar stripes around its neck, like a necklace.
They love to bask on big rocks in the hot sun.
desert_cottontail: They are most active at dawn and dusk when it's cooler.
Their big ears help let out heat so they stay cool in hot weather.
desert_horned_lizard: They eat lots of ants, licking them up with their sticky tongues.
They can puff up their bodies to look bigger and harder to swallow.
desert_iguana: Desert iguanas eat mostly flowers and leaves, especially yellow creosote blossoms.
Their pale color helps reflect the hot desert sun.
desert_millipede: It comes out after summer rains, when the desert is damp.
It eats dead leaves and plants, helping recycle them into soil.
desert_tortoise: They can store water in their bladder to help survive long dry spells.
Desert tortoises dig burrows with their strong, flat front legs.
diamondback_terrapin: The rings on each shell plate look like diamonds, which gives them their name.
They have special glands near their eyes that help get rid of extra salt.
diamondback_watersnake: It has a pattern of dark chain-like diamonds along its back.
Diamondback watersnakes often bask on branches hanging over the water.
dickcissel: Males have a black V on a yellow chest, like a little meadowlark.
They fly in big flocks to spend the winter in South America.
differential_grasshopper: Grasshoppers hear with ear-like spots on the sides of their bellies.
They lay eggs in the soil in fall, and the babies hatch in spring.
domestic_cat: They have whiskers that help them feel their way and judge if they fit through a gap.
They spend a big part of each day sleeping, often 12 hours or more.
domestic_chicken: Chickens can recognize many different faces, including other chickens and people.
Mother hens cluck to their chicks while they are still inside the egg.
domestic_dog: Dogs have a sense of smell many thousands of times better than people do.
Each dog's nose print has a unique pattern, just like a human fingerprint.
domestic_rabbit: Rabbits' teeth never stop growing, so they chew hay to keep them short.
Happy rabbits sometimes jump and twist in the air, which is called a binky.
dotted_periwinkle: They graze on tiny algae growing on rocks, scraping it with a rough tongue.
They can close up their shell with a little trapdoor to keep from drying out.
double_crested_cormorant: The 'double crest' is two little tufts of feathers on its head during breeding season.
douglass_ground_squirrel: They have a dark wedge-shaped patch of fur between their shoulders.
They live in colonies and give sharp alarm calls when danger is near.
douglass_squirrel: They are also called chickarees, after the sound of their chattering calls.
They often eat cones at one favorite spot, leaving big piles of cone scales.
downy_woodpecker: They often visit backyard feeders and love suet.
Males have a small red patch on the back of the head; females do not.
dungeness_crab: Dungeness crabs bury themselves in sand with just their eyes peeking out.
They have ten legs, and the front two are big claws.
dunlin: In spring it gets a black patch on its belly that looks like it sat in mud.
It probes the mud with its drooping bill to find worms and tiny shellfish.
dunns_salamander: Like other woodland salamanders, it has no lungs and breathes through its damp skin.
Like its relatives, its babies hatch from eggs on land, already looking like tiny adults.
dusky_grouse: Males have colorful bare skin patches on their necks that they show off in spring.
In winter they eat mostly the needles of fir and other conifer trees.
dusky_surgeonfish: Surgeonfish graze on algae, helping keep coral reefs clean.
Dusky surgeonfish are small, dark brown fish that often swim in groups.
eastern_amberwing: Males have amber-orange wings, which gives this dragonfly its name.
Its striped body may help it look like a wasp, which keeps birds away.
eastern_blacknose_dace: It has a dark stripe running from its nose along its side, giving it its name.
In spring, males get a rusty orange color along their sides.
eastern_bluebird: Males are bright blue on top with a rusty-orange chest.
Young birds from an earlier nest sometimes help their parents feed new babies.
eastern_box_turtle: Eastern box turtles often have bright yellow and orange patterns on their shells.
They love to munch on berries, mushrooms and worms.
eastern_boxelder_bug: They are black with red-orange stripes and mostly sip juice from boxelder trees.
They are harmless to people and do not hurt houses.
eastern_calligrapher: Like other hover flies, it can hover in one spot in midair like a tiny helicopter.
Its larvae eat aphids, so it helps protect garden plants.
eastern_carpenter_bee: Males cannot sting, though they buzz around boldly to guard their area.
They look like bumble bees but have a shiny, mostly hairless black belly.
eastern_chipmunk: Chipmunks make a 'chip-chip' sound that gives them their name.
Chipmunks spend winter in their burrows, waking up now and then to snack on stored food.
eastern_collared_lizard: Males can be bright blue-green with yellow heads and black collars.
They bask on rocks and eat grasshoppers and other insects.
eastern_copperhead: Baby copperheads have bright yellow-green tail tips.
They sense body heat with small pits on their face, helping them find mice in the dark.
eastern_cottontail: They are named for their fluffy white tails, which look like cotton balls.
Their eyes are on the sides of their heads, so they can see almost all the way around.
eastern_fence_lizard: Eastern fence lizards are often seen basking on fence posts, which gave them their name.
Males have shiny blue patches on their bellies and throats.
eastern_forktail: Young females are bright orange, then turn a bluish-gray as they grow up.
Males have a green body and a bright blue tip on their tail.
eastern_foxsnake: It gets its name from a musky smell some people say is like a fox.
They are good climbers and swimmers and often live near marshes and fields.
eastern_gray_squirrel: They use their bushy tails like an umbrella, a blanket and a balance pole.
They can rotate their back ankles to climb down trees headfirst.
eastern_hellbender: Hellbenders live in clean, fast-flowing streams with big rocks to hide under.
A hellbender's main food is crayfish.
eastern_hognose_snake: Its upturned snout works like a shovel for digging in sandy soil.
Hognose snakes love to eat toads.
eastern_kingbird: It has a neat white band at the tip of its black tail.
It spends the winter in South America, where it eats lots of fruit.
eastern_kingsnake: They are shiny black with thin white or yellow bands that look like a chain.
Some people call them chain kingsnakes because of their chain-link pattern.
eastern_lubber_grasshopper: Eastern lubber grasshoppers are big and slow, so they mostly walk and hop instead of fly.
Their bright colors warn hungry animals that they taste terrible.
eastern_meadow_vole: They have short tails, tiny ears and are busy all year, even under the snow.
They eat grasses and seeds and are food for owls, hawks and foxes.
eastern_milksnake: Its name comes from an old myth that it drank milk from cows, which is not true.
Milksnakes are close cousins of kingsnakes and are active mostly at night.
eastern_mole: Its huge front feet are shaped like shovels for digging through soil.
Its tiny eyes are hidden in fur, and it finds food mostly by touch and smell.
eastern_mosquitofish: Mosquitofish give birth to live babies instead of laying eggs.
Their mouths point upward, which is great for grabbing food at the water's surface.
eastern_mud_turtle: Mud turtles spend lots of time walking on land, not just swimming.
They often bury themselves in mud during dry or cold times.
eastern_musk_turtle: They rarely bask and usually walk along the bottom of ponds instead of swimming.
They have two light stripes on each side of the head.
eastern_narrow_mouthed_toad: It has a small pointy head and a fold of skin behind its eyes.
It loves to eat ants and can close the skin fold to protect its eyes from bites.
eastern_newt: Eastern newts have bright red spots on their backs with black borders.
Their skin has a bad taste that keeps most hungry animals away.
eastern_phoebe: It often builds its mud nest under bridges or on porches.
It says its own name: 'fee-bee, fee-bee!'
eastern_pondhawk: They are fierce little hunters that catch other flying insects in midair.
Young pondhawks live underwater for months before becoming flying adults.
eastern_ratsnake: Young ratsnakes have blotchy patterns that change as they grow up.
They help farmers by eating mice and rats.
eastern_ratsnake_pantherophis: When nervous, ratsnakes may shake their tails in dry leaves to make a buzzing sound.
Young ratsnakes have blotchy patterns that change as they grow up.
eastern_red_backed_salamander: Some have a red stripe down their backs, while others are all dark gray.
They lay eggs on land, and babies hatch as tiny salamanders, not tadpoles.
eastern_red_bat: Unlike most bats, moms often have twins, triplets or even quadruplets.
They wrap their furry tails around themselves like a blanket in cold weather.
eastern_spadefoot: Its eyes have up-and-down slit pupils, like a cat's.
It can stay buried underground for long times and comes out after heavy rains.
eastern_tailed_blue: Eastern tailed-blue males are bright blue on top, while females are mostly gray-brown.
Their caterpillars eat clover and other plants in the pea family.
eastern_tent_caterpillar_moth: Its caterpillars leave silk trails so their brothers and sisters can find the way home.
The adult moths are brown and fuzzy and only live a few days.
eastern_tiger_salamander: They are among the largest land salamanders in North America.
In early spring they walk to ponds, often on rainy nights, to lay their eggs.
eastern_tiger_swallowtail: Its young caterpillars look like bird droppings, which keeps hungry birds away.
They often visit flowers in gardens, parks and along forest edges.
eastern_towhee: Its call sounds like it's saying 'drink-your-tea!'
Male eastern towhees have black backs, rusty sides, and bright white bellies.
ebony_jewelwing: Ebony jewelwings flutter like butterflies along shady forest streams.
Females have a small white spot near the tip of each wing.
elk: Males grow huge antlers every year and drop them in late winter or spring.
In fall, males make a loud, high call called a bugle.
empress_leilia: Males like to perch on sunny spots and fly out to check on anything passing by.
Its wings are warm orange-brown with dark eyespots near the edges.
ensatina: Ensatinas have a tail that is skinny where it joins the body, so it can drop off to escape.
Ensatina moms guard their eggs in a damp hiding spot until they hatch.
eurasian_collared_dove: It has a thin black ring on the back of its neck, like a collar.
european_carp: Carp use whisker-like barbels near their mouth to feel for food in mud.
Goldfish and carp are close cousins in the same family.
european_firebug: Most firebugs have tiny wings and cannot fly, so they walk everywhere.
They often sun themselves in groups at the base of trees and walls.
european_green_crab: Green crabs came from Europe long ago, likely hitching a ride on ships.
Green crabs are tough and can live in both cold and warm water.
european_mantis: It can be green or brown to blend in with leaves and grass.
Females lay eggs in a foamy case that hardens and protects them through winter.
european_paper_wasp: Their open nests look like upside-down umbrellas full of six-sided cells.
Only the queens survive the winter, and each one starts a new nest in spring.
european_starling: Huge flocks can swirl through the sky together in shapes called murmurations.
Their feathers are shiny with green and purple colors that sparkle in sunlight.
fall_webworm_moth: Fall webworm moths are bright white, and some have little dark spots on their wings.
Their caterpillars are fuzzy and can be yellowish or dark.
fantail_darter: Like other darters, it has no swim bladder, so it rests on the stream bottom.
It darts quickly from rock to rock in fast, shallow streams.
fathead_minnow: The male lays out a nest under a rock or log and keeps the eggs clean.
When one gets hurt, it releases a scent that warns other minnows to hide.
fatmucket: Like other freshwater mussels, it uses a muscle called a foot to move and dig.
Its shell is shiny yellowish-brown on the outside and pearly white inside.
fiery_skipper: Fiery skipper caterpillars eat grasses and are often found in lawns.
Fiery skippers have short antennae with little hooks at the ends.
fisher: Fishers can turn their back feet around to climb down trees headfirst.
They are a large member of the weasel family.
five_lined_skink: Adult males get orange-red heads in spring.
Moms stay with their eggs and guard them until they hatch.
flame_skimmer: Males perch on sticks near the water and guard their favorite spots.
They are often seen near warm ponds and streams, even ones in hot dry places.
florida_bass: Florida bass have a huge mouth that stretches past their eyes.
They like warm, weedy lakes and hide near plants waiting for a meal.
florida_cottonmouth: It is a strong swimmer and often floats high on top of the water.
It can sense the warmth of animals with special pits on its face.
florida_gar: Gars are an ancient kind of fish whose family has been around since the time of dinosaurs.
Their scales are hard and shiny, like a suit of armor.
florida_red_bellied_cooter: They love to bask in the sun on logs, sometimes stacked up together.
Females sometimes lay their eggs inside alligator nests.
florida_softshell_turtle: It is one of the biggest softshell turtles in North America.
It likes to bury itself in sand or mud, with only its head poking out.
forsters_tern: In winter, they have a black eye patch that looks like a mask.
They often build nests on floating mats of marsh plants.
fowlers_toad: Look for three or more warts in each dark spot on its back.
They are most active at night and hide in sandy burrows by day.
fox_squirrel: They are the biggest tree squirrels in North America.
Their fur colors can range from orange-brown to gray to almost all black.
fragile_forktail: Fragile forktails are tiny damselflies with thin bodies like a needle.
They have pale little marks on their shoulders that look like exclamation points.
fragile_papershell: Like other freshwater mussels, it cleans river water by filtering it.
Its babies ride on the gills of fish for a while before settling on the river bottom.
franklins_ground_squirrel: They live in tall grass and are harder to spot than other ground squirrels.
Its call is a clear musical whistle, unlike the chirps of many ground squirrels.
fremonts_squirrel: It is a small, chattering tree squirrel that lives in mountain pine forests.
It loudly scolds visitors with chirps and chatters from the treetops.
frilled_dogwinkle: Its shell often has wavy frills or ridges that give it its name.
Dogwinkles lay eggs in tiny yellow capsules that look like grains of rice.
fuzzy_horned_bumble_bee: Like all bumble bees, only the queens survive winter, resting underground.
Their orange-tipped back end helps tell them apart from other bumble bees.
gadwall: They often snatch plants that diving ducks and coots bring up from the bottom.
Females quack like mallards, while males make a low, burpy call.
gambels_quail: They have a fun teardrop-shaped feather plume that bobs on top of their heads.
Families often walk together in groups called coveys.
garden_snail: Garden snails carry their shell homes everywhere and pull inside to stay safe and moist.
Their eyes sit on the tips of their long upper tentacles.
garibaldi: Its babies are orange with bright blue spots that fade as they grow.
Adults are bright orange all over and stay close to their own rocky home.
german_cockroach: They are fast runners and can squeeze into cracks as thin as a coin.
Mother cockroaches carry an egg case on their back end until the babies are ready to hatch.
giant_desert_centipede: It is one of the biggest centipedes in North America.
Its bright colors warn other animals to leave it alone, so it is best watched from afar.
giant_floater: Its shell is thin and light, which helps it stay on top of soft mud.
Like other mussels, it cleans water by filtering out tiny bits of food.
giant_green_anemone: It catches food with sticky, stinging tentacles and pulls it into its mouth.
It can live for many decades in the same rocky spot.
giant_house_spider: They can run very quickly across the floor on their long legs.
They are shy and would much rather hide than meet people.
gila_woodpecker: After they move out, other birds like owls and flycatchers often move into their old holes.
Males have a small round red cap on the top of the head.
glaucous_gull: Glaucous gulls spend summers in the Arctic, far to the north.
Young glaucous gulls are a pale, creamy color, almost all white.
glaucous_winged_gull: Its wingtips are gray instead of black like many other gulls.
Young gulls are brown and take about four years to get their adult colors.
gold_dust_day_gecko: They have sticky toe pads that let them walk up walls and even glass.
Golden speckles on their green back look like they were sprinkled with gold dust.
golden_crayfish: They live under rocks in streams and rivers.
Like other crayfish, they can grow back a lost claw or leg.
golden_crowned_sparrow: It has a bright yellow patch on top of its head, framed by black stripes.
Golden-crowned sparrows nest up north and spend winter farther south.
golden_eagle: Golden feathers on the back of their heads give them their name.
They build huge stick nests on cliffs and use them year after year.
golden_hamster: Hamsters stuff food into stretchy cheek pouches to carry it home.
They are most active at night and love to run, dig and burrow.
golden_silk_spider: Females are much bigger than males, which are tiny in comparison.

goldenrod_soldier_beetle: Goldenrod soldier beetles help flowers by carrying pollen from bloom to bloom.

goldeye: Its big eyes help it see in cloudy, muddy rivers.

goldfish: Goldfish can learn to recognize the person who feeds them.

gooseneck_barnacle: They live in big clusters on rocks pounded by ocean waves.

gopher_snake: Gopher snakes are great at catching mice and gophers, which helps farmers.

gopher_tortoise: They dig with flat, shovel-like front legs.

gray_catbird: Catbirds have a hidden rusty-red patch under their tail.

gray_fox: They have a black stripe running down the top of their bushy tail.

gray_hairstreak: Gray hairstreaks have an orange spot near their tails on the underside of their wings.

gray_sea_star: It buries itself in the sand just under the surface.

gray_treefrog: They have bright yellow-orange patches on the inside of their back legs.

gray_wolf: Wolves live in family groups called packs.

great_basin_spadefoot: A hard, dark 'spade' on each back foot helps it dig backward into the soil.

great_black_backed_gull: It takes about four years for young gulls to get their black-and-white adult feathers.
great_blue_heron: They fly with their necks tucked in an S-shape and long legs trailing behind.

great_frigatebird: Its wings are so long and light that it can stay in the air for weeks.

great_horned_owl: Its ear tufts are just feathers, and its real ears are hidden on the sides of its head.

great_plains_skink: They are one of the biggest skinks in North America.

great_plains_toad: Its back is covered with big dark blotches outlined in light color.

great_spangled_fritillary: Its caterpillars eat only violet plants.

great_tailed_grackle: They gather in huge, noisy flocks to sleep in trees at night.

greater_earless_lizard: As the name says, it has no outside ear openings.

greater_roadrunner: Greater roadrunners can fly, but they would rather run.

greater_short_horned_lizard: Its flat, round body helps it soak up the sun.

greater_yellowlegs: As its name says, it has long, bright yellow legs for wading in water.

green_and_black_poison_dart_frog: The father often carries tadpoles on his back to small pools of water.

green_anole: Green anoles have sticky toe pads that help them climb leaves and walls.

green_frog: A male's round eardrum is bigger than his eye.

green_heron: When excited, it raises a shaggy crest on its head.

green_iguana: They are good swimmers and can dive into water to escape danger.

green_sea_turtle: Green sea turtles are named for the green color of their fat, not their shells.

green_sunfish: It has a big mouth and a black spot on its gill cover.

green_treefrog: They have sticky toe pads that help them climb plants and windows.

green_winged_teal: Males have a shiny green stripe behind each eye on a chestnut head.

greenhouse_frog: Greenhouse frogs are tiny, about the size of a fingertip.

greenhouse_millipede: It came from Asia and now lives in gardens and greenhouses around the world.

greenside_darter: Darters rest on the stream bottom and dart quickly from spot to spot.

grey_francolin: They often live in small family groups.

grey_seal: Grey seal pups are born with fluffy white fur.

groundhog: They are also called woodchucks and are a kind of big ground squirrel.

gulf_coast_buck_moth: Its spiny caterpillars munch on oak leaves, so it is best to just look at them.

gulf_coast_toad: They have a dark stripe along each side and bony ridges on top of the head.

gulf_fritillary: Gulf fritillary caterpillars are bright orange with black spines.

gulf_longear_sunfish: Like other longear sunfish, males build round gravel nests and guard the eggs.

gunnisons_prairie_dog: Unlike some prairie dogs, they hibernate during winter.

hackberry_emperor: Their caterpillars eat only hackberry tree leaves, which gave them their name.

hairy_woodpecker: Hairy woodpeckers look like downy woodpeckers but have a much longer bill.

halloween_pennant: It perches on tall plant tips and flaps like a little flag in the wind.

harbor_seal: Harbor seals can sleep underwater and pop up to breathe without fully waking.

harbour_porpoise: They are one of the smallest whales and dolphins in the ocean.

harlequin_duck: Male harlequin ducks have fancy white stripes and spots like a painted clown.

harris_antelope_squirrel: They have a white stripe along each side of their body.

harriss_sparrow: Adults have a black face and bib and a pink bill.

hawai_i_amakihi: It is a small yellow-green bird found on islands and nowhere else in the world.

hawaiian_black_nerite: Hawaiian black nerites graze on tiny algae that grow on wet rocks.

hawaiian_convict_surgeonfish: Its black stripes look like a striped uniform, which is how it got its name.

hawaiian_coot: It is found only in Hawaii and nowhere else on Earth.

hawaiian_garden_spider: It sits in the middle of its web, often upside down, waiting for insects.

hawaiian_goose: The nene is the rarest goose in the world.

hawaiian_hoary_bat: It roosts alone in trees instead of living in caves.

hawaiian_monk_seal: They love to nap on sandy beaches, so people give them plenty of space.

hawaiian_snakehead_cowrie: Its shell has a dark middle and white speckles, a bit like a snake's head.

hawaiian_spotted_toby: Hawaiian spotted tobies are brown with lots of little white spots.

hermit_thrush: It flicks its rusty tail up and then slowly lowers it.

hickory_tussock_moth: Its caterpillars often feed in groups on hickory and walnut trees.

highland_stoneroller: They have a hard ridge on their lower jaw for scraping algae off rocks.

hispid_cotton_rat: Its fur is coarse and bristly, which is what 'hispid' means.

hoary_marmot: Their silver-gray fur gives them the name 'hoary,' which means grayish.

hooded_merganser: Their thin bills have saw-like edges that help them grip slippery fish.

hopi_chipmunk: It has orange-brown fur with soft stripes down its back.

horned_nudibranch: It is a sea slug with bright orange and blue colors.

horned_puffin: It has a small black fleshy horn above each eye, which gives it its name.

horse: Horses can sleep standing up by locking their legs in place.

house_centipede: House centipedes are very fast and can run across a room in a flash.

house_finch: House finches spread across the East after pet birds were set free there.

house_fly: House flies taste food with their feet.

house_mouse: Their whiskers help them feel their way around in the dark.

house_sparrow: House sparrows love to take dust baths to keep their feathers clean.

humpback_whale: Its long flippers can be about one-third as long as its whole body.

hunts_bumble_bee: Its fuzzy body has bright orange-red bands in the middle.

huron_skipper: Like other skippers, it holds its wings partly open when resting, like a jet plane.

i_iwi: Its bright red feathers and curved pink bill make it easy to spot.

indigo_bunting: They migrate at night and use the stars to find their way.

indo_pacific_rock_boring_urchin: Like other sea urchins, it walks with hundreds of tiny tube feet.

isabella_tiger_moth: Some people say the woolly bear's stripes can predict winter, but that is just a fun myth.

italian_wall_lizard: Italian wall lizards are often bright green on the back with brown or dark markings.

jacksons_chameleon: It catches bugs with a sticky tongue that can be longer than its body.

japanese_beetle: They came to the US from Japan, where natural enemies keep them in check.

java_sparrow: It is a kind of finch, and in the wild it loves to eat rice and other seeds.

johnny_darter: Johnny darters don't have a swim bladder, so they rest on the stream bottom.

jonah_crab: Their shells are reddish on top and yellowish underneath.

joro_spider: Females are big with yellow, blue-black and red colors, while males are tiny and brown.

kalij_pheasant: Females are brown and speckled, which helps them hide on the forest floor.

killdeer: Killdeer are named after their loud call, which sounds like 'kill-deer'.

ladder_backed_woodpecker: Males have a red cap on top of the head, and females don't.

lake_trout: Lake trout like very cold water and swim deep in lakes during summer.

lapland_longspur: They have a very long claw on their back toe, which gives them their name.

large_creosote_gall_midge: Gall midges are tiny flies, smaller than a grain of rice.

large_yellow_underwing: It came from Europe and has spread across North America.

largemouth_bass: They often hide near logs and weeds, waiting for food to swim by.

largescale_stoneroller: They scrape algae off rocks with a hard ridge on their lower jaw.

lark_sparrow: Lark sparrows have a bold face pattern with chestnut, black and white stripes.

laughing_gull: In summer its head turns black, and in winter it turns mostly white.

laysan_albatross: Its wings can stretch over 6 feet from tip to tip.

lazuli_bunting: Males are bright blue on top with an orange chest and white belly.

leafy_spurge_hawkmoth: Its caterpillar is colorful with spots and stripes in red, black, and yellow.

least_chipmunk: Least chipmunks can climb trees but spend most of their time on the ground.

leather_star: It is usually blue-gray with orange-red patches.

lesser_goldfinch: They are one of the smallest finches in North America.

ligated_furrow_bee: Ligated furrow bees are small bees that sometimes live and work together in families.

limpkin: Its long curved bill is shaped to pull snails out of their shells.

lined_chiton: Its shell plates are striped with zigzag lines of pink, red, and blue.

lined_shore_crab: They scurry sideways across rocks and hide in cracks when danger comes.

little_blue_heron: Little blue herons walk slowly in shallow water to hunt for fish and frogs.

little_brown_skink: It wiggles like a tiny snake through leaves on the forest floor.

loggerhead_sea_turtle: They have big heads and strong jaws to crunch crabs and clams.

long_toed_salamander: It has a yellow or green stripe down its dark back.

longear_sunfish: It has a long black flap on its gill cover that looks like an ear.

longfin_dace: They can survive dry times by hiding in wet sand or under damp plants.

lorquins_admiral: It has black wings with white bands and bright orange wingtips.

luna_moth: Its bright green wings help it hide among leaves.

magnificent_bryozoan: Each tiny animal in the colony has a ring of tentacles to catch food from the water.

mallard: Males have shiny green heads, while females are mottled brown.

mapleleaf: Mapleleaf mussels filter the water they live in, which helps keep rivers clean.

marbled_murrelet: In summer it turns a mottled brown, and in winter it is black and white.

marbled_salamander: It has bold black and white or silvery bands, like a marble countertop.

margined_calligrapher: Its larvae eat aphids, helping protect garden plants.

marine_blue: Marine blues are tiny butterflies with purple-blue wings on top.

marsh_rabbit: Marsh rabbits have shorter ears and smaller feet than most other rabbits.

mayan_cichlid: It has a big dark spot ringed with color near its tail, like a fake eye.

mediterranean_house_gecko: They often hang around porch lights at night to catch bugs.

melissa_blue: Melissa blue males are bright blue, while females are brown with orange bands.

mexican_free_tailed_bat: They live in huge colonies, and some caves hold millions of bats.

milberts_tortoiseshell: Its caterpillars feed on stinging nettle plants.

milkweed_tussock_moth: Its caterpillars have tufts of orange, black and white hairs.

mississippi_kite: They are graceful gray hawks that often fly in groups.

mississippi_slimy_salamander: Mississippi slimy salamanders are black with tiny white or silver specks.

monarch: Its caterpillars only eat milkweed plants.

moonglow_anemone: Its tentacles have tiny stingers that help it catch small animals.

moorish_idol: It has bold black, white and yellow stripes that make it easy to spot.

moose: Only male moose grow antlers, and they grow a new pair every year.

mormon_cricket: They can't fly, so they march across the land on foot.

mormon_fritillary: It's one of the smaller fritillaries, orange with black spots on top.
mottled_snake_eyed_skink: It cannot blink, so it licks its eyes to keep them clean.

mottled_star: Mottled stars have long, skinny arms and come in colors like gray, brown, green and orange.

mountain_bluebird: They nest in tree holes and birdhouses.

mountain_chickadee: It has a white stripe over its eye, like an eyebrow.

mountain_cottontail: Its white fluffy tail looks like a cotton ball, which gives it its name.

mourning_gecko: It has sticky toe pads that let it walk up walls and windows.

mud_fiddler_crab: They dig burrows in mud and hide inside when the tide comes in.

mule_deer: They bounce on all four feet at once, which is called stotting.

muskox: Muskoxen have a super soft underwool called qiviut that's warmer than sheep's wool.

muskrat: They can hold their breath underwater for many minutes.

mute_swan: They hold their necks in a graceful S curve and often arch their wings.

neotropic_cormorant: They have long hooked bills and dive underwater to chase fish.

north_american_porcupine: North American porcupines are good climbers and often rest high in trees.
north_american_racer: It holds its head up high off the ground to look around.

north_american_river_otter: River otters love to play and slide down muddy or snowy banks.

north_american_wheel_bug: It is one of the biggest true bugs in North America.

northern_acorn_barnacle: Barnacles stick out feathery legs to catch tiny food floating in the water.

northern_alligator_lizard: Unlike many lizards, mothers give birth to live babies.

northern_bay_mussel: They live packed together in big groups called mussel beds.

northern_cardinal: Male cardinals often feed seeds to females, which looks like a kiss.

northern_cottonmouth: Northern cottonmouths are also called water moccasins and love swamps and slow streams.

northern_cricket_frog: It is a tiny frog, about the size of a fingertip.

northern_curly_tailed_lizard: They came to the US from the Bahamas and nearby islands.

northern_dusky_salamander: It has a light line from its eye to the corner of its jaw.

northern_elephant_seal: Male elephant seals have big droopy noses that look a bit like an elephant's trunk.

northern_flicker: Flickers have bright yellow or red feathers under their wings and tails.

northern_harrier: They fly low over fields with their wings held up in a V.

northern_house_wren: They often stick their tails straight up as they hop around.

northern_kelp_crab: Northern kelp crabs are often olive green or reddish to match the seaweed they live in.

northern_leopard_frog: It has dark round spots on green or brown skin, like a leopard.

northern_map_turtle: Females are much larger than males.

northern_mockingbird: It flashes white wing patches when it flies or shows off.

northern_paper_wasp: Their nests look like upside-down umbrellas with many six-sided cells.

northern_pike: Pike have long, torpedo-shaped bodies built for quick bursts of speed.

northern_pintail: Males have a white stripe running up the side of their brown head.

northern_red_bellied_cooter: It loves to bask on logs in the sun, sometimes stacked with other turtles.

northern_red_legged_frog: Northern red-legged frogs often lay their eggs in winter or early spring.

northern_rubber_boa: Its skin feels soft and smooth, a bit like rubber.

northern_short_tailed_shrew: Its tiny eyes don't see well, so it finds its way with smell, touch, and squeaks.
